changes: pads: none → pads (groove_mm 3, lip_mm 0, pad_angle_deg 0, pad_tpu_mm 1.5, reach_mm 0, width_mm 12)
why: The slide fixes geometry for every width, and the grooved TPU pads (pad angle 0, as the slide does not turn) trap the balls and fruit that flat faces can let roll. Total $5.40, 3 days, 176 machine minutes, within budget.

A 10 deg tilt (between the other two proposals) handles the round objects. Widening the pad from 12 to 16 mm gives the long, heavy sugar box more resistance to tipping. The earlier 24 mm trial also changed the groove from 3 to 6 mm, and the deeper groove most likely caused its losses (wood cube, marker, potted meat). Keeping the groove at 3 mm and widening only modestly tests the width alone. Reprint about 20 min, $0.

With R = 26-37 mm on a 16 mm pad (w = 8), the rims sit 16 mm apart and lean in by only 12-18 deg. At 20 mm (w = 10) the sagitta is still under 3 mm for every fruit (1.4-1.9 mm), so they keep bridging the rims. Those rims are now 20 mm apart and lean in by 16-23 deg, which gives more centring and about 25% more torsional resistance against the roll. The record supports width as the lever. Going 12 to 16 mm in iteration 3 gained racquetball, strawberry and golf_ball, all round objects. The one wider trial (24 mm) also deepened the groove to 6 mm, and iteration 3 traced its small-object losses to the depth. So I keep the groove at 3 mm and widen modestly. Nothing to buy; about 1 g more PLA/TPU.
